objectives: Students should use cumulative frequency graphs to determine how many data values fall below or above certain thresholds (Maths 6.1)
Students should interpret cumulative frequency graphs to compare distributions (Maths 6.1)
Students should estimate the median, quartiles, and interquartile range from cumulative frequency graphs (Maths 6.1)

keyConcepts.concept: Using cumulative frequency graphs to find data values
keyConcepts.explanation: Cumulative frequency graphs show the total number of data points below a particular value, allowing you to find how many data points lie below or above a given threshold.

keyConcepts.concept: Comparing distributions using cumulative frequency graphs
keyConcepts.explanation: By comparing the shape and spread of cumulative frequency graphs for different data sets, you can analyze differences in distributions such as spread and central tendency.

keyConcepts.concept: Estimating median, quartiles, and interquartile range from cumulative frequency graphs
keyConcepts.explanation: The median corresponds to the value at 50% cumulative frequency, quartiles correspond to 25% and 75% cumulative frequencies, and the interquartile range is the difference between the upper and lower quartiles.

steps.title: Introduction to Cumulative Frequency Graphs
steps.content: Cumulative frequency graphs are used to display the cumulative total of frequencies up to each class boundary. They help us find out how many data values are below or above certain values, compare distributions, and estimate important statistics like medians and quartiles.

steps.title: Multiple Choice Question: Reading Values from a Cumulative Frequency Graph
steps.content: If a cumulative frequency graph shows a cumulative frequency of 40 at a value of 30, what does this mean?

questions.question: What does the cumulative frequency of 40 at the value 30 tell us?
options: There are 40 data points with values less than or equal to 30
There are 30 data points with values less than or equal to 40
There are 40 data points with values greater than 30
There are 30 data points with values greater than 40
questions.explanation: The cumulative frequency at 30 tells us how many data points have values less than or equal to 30.

steps.content: The interquartile range is calculated by subtracting the __[dropdown1]__ quartile from the __[dropdown2]__ quartile. These correspond to the __[dropdown3]__ and __[dropdown4]__ percentiles respectively.

steps.title: Practice Question: Using a Cumulative Frequency Graph
steps.content: A cumulative frequency graph shows a total of 60 data points. The cumulative frequency at 40 is 45 and at 55 is 58. Estimate the number of data points between 40 and 55.

questions.question: What is the estimated number of data points with values between 40 and 55?
questions.explanation: The number of data points between 40 and 55 is the difference of cumulative frequencies: 58 - 45 = 13.
